seoTitle: Free Docker Compose Environment Generator from .env
metaDescription: Generate a compose environment block or env_file setup from a .env file, or extract variables from a docker-compose.yml into .env.example. Free.
intro: Works both ways: from a .env file it writes a compose "environment:" block with ${VAR:-default} interpolation or an env_file entry, and from a docker-compose.yml it extracts variables into a .env.example.
why: Compose files and .env files drift apart. A new variable gets added to one and forgotten in the other, and someone spends an hour finding out why a container starts without its password. This helper keeps them in step. Give it a .env and it writes the environment section for a service, with ${VAR:-default} interpolation so the file works with or without a local .env, or an env_file reference instead. Give it a docker-compose.yml and it collects every ${VAR}, ${VAR:-default} and environment key into a ready .env.example. Which direction applies is your choice in the mode menu. Everything is processed in your browser, so config containing passwords is not uploaded.
howTo: Choose the mode: .env to compose environment, .env to compose env_file, or compose to .env.example.
Paste the .env file or the docker-compose.yml into the input box and set the service name.
Decide whether to use ${VAR:-default} interpolation, then copy the result.

faq.a: Each variable is written as ${NAME:-default}, using the value from your .env as the default. Compose then reads NAME from the environment or a .env file, and falls back to the default.

faq.q: What does the compose to .env.example mode collect?
faq.a: Every ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} reference, and the keys under environment, so the example file lists everything the stack can be configured with.

faq.q: Does it hide secrets in the default values?
faq.a: No. Defaults are written as they appear in your .env. Use the .env sanitizer first if the values are real secrets.

faq.q: When should I use env_file instead?
faq.a: env_file keeps the compose file short and loads every variable from a file. Explicit environment entries document what the service needs. Choose what suits your team.
